prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `tasklist` extension and registered it, so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works. The full test suite passes (1141 tests, 112 skipped); flake8 isn't installed, so it was not run. List items starting with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` plus a space get a checkbox, which is disabled unless `clickable` is true, and the item gets the `item_class` class (default `task`). This works in ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists, and inline markup after the marker still renders. The marker is removed before links are parsed, so `[x]` is never read as a link. In a loose list the checkbox goes at the start of the item's first paragraph. With the default XHTML output it renders as `disabled="disabled"`; with `output_format='html'` it renders as plain `checked disabled`. I also added docs, a changelog entry under `[unreleased]` and an API reference page.
